retaliation_rule: Except where the tenant owes one week's rent or more, it is a defence to a possessory action on residential property that the action was in retaliation for the tenant (I) reporting a violation (or what he reasonably and in good faith believes is a violation) of RSA 540-A or an unreasonable and substantial violation of a regulation/housing code to the landlord or an inspecting authority, (II) initiating a good-faith action under RSA 540-A or using the procedure of 540:13-d, or (III) meeting with other tenants for any lawful purpose (RSA 540:13-a). No time-based presumption.

deposit_max: 1.5 times one month's rent. If the landlord collects more security later, the extra collected in any year may not exceed 10% of the current deposit (46:8-21.2). The deposit stays the tenant's money, held in trust and not mixed with the landlord's own funds; it must sit in an interest-bearing account at a New Jersey bank or savings institution (landlords with 10+ units: an insured money-market fund or variable-rate account) (46:8-19(a), (b)).
deposit_interest: Yes. The interest belongs to the tenant and is paid each year in cash or credited toward rent on the lease renewal or anniversary (or each January 31 after written notice). Within 30 days of receiving the deposit (and on moving it, on each annual interest payment and on sale of the property) the landlord must tell the tenant in writing the bank's name and address, account type, interest rate and amount. If the landlord fails to invest the deposit, give the notice or pay interest, the tenant may give written notice and apply the deposit plus 7% annual interest to rent, and the landlord can't demand a new deposit; for a missed annual payment or notice the landlord first gets 30 days to fix it (46:8-19(c)).
late_fee_rule: No statewide cap on late fees for ordinary tenants was found in the statutes. Tenants who are senior citizens receiving Social Security Old Age, Railroad Retirement or other government pensions, or who receive SSDI, SSI or Work First New Jersey benefits, get a grace period of five business days (excluding weekends and State or federal holidays) when rent is due on the 1st, and no late charge may be made that includes the grace period (2A:42-6.1, 6.3). A landlord who violates this is a disorderly person (2A:42-6.2). In a nonpayment eviction, if the tenant pays all rent due within 3 business days after the warrant for removal is posted, no late fee above the amount in the warrant application may be charged (2A:42-10.16a).
entry_notice: No general landlord-entry notice statute was found. A state regulation for multiple dwellings (buildings with 3+ units) says the tenant must give the owner or agent access for code inspections and needed repairs 'upon reasonable notification, which under ordinary circumstances shall be one day', and immediate access in safety or structural emergencies (N.J.A.C. 5:10-5.1(c); multiple dwelling defined in N.J.S.A. 55:13A-3). Hotels: immediate access.
month_to_month_tenant_notice: No New Jersey statute found that sets how much notice a tenant must give to end a month-to-month tenancy. Check the lease. A tenant who holds over after a lease of one month or longer becomes a month-to-month tenant if the landlord accepts rent (46:8-10).
month_to_month_landlord_notice: Most residential tenants are covered by the Anti-Eviction Act: the landlord may not evict or refuse to renew except for one of the listed good causes (2A:18-61.1, 61.3), and the end of the term alone is not enough. The written notice depends on the cause: 3 days (disorderly conduct, damage, certain crimes), one month (rule or lease violations after a notice to cease, habitual late payment, refusing reasonable lease changes), 3 months (code-violation removal), 2 months (owner occupancy in buildings of 3 or fewer units), 18 months (retiring the building), 3 years (condo/co-op conversion) (2A:18-61.2). Not covered: owner-occupied buildings with no more than 2 rental units, plus seasonal and transient rentals; for these, a month-to-month tenancy ends with one month's notice to quit (2A:18-56(b)).
rent_increase_notice: No statewide notice period in days for rent increases was found in the statutes. A covered tenant can be evicted for not paying an increase only after a valid notice to quit and notice of the increase, and only if the increase isn't unconscionable and complies with any other laws or municipal ordinances that govern rent increases (2A:18-61.1(f)). The landlord can also propose reasonable lease changes when the lease ends (2A:18-61.1(i), with one month's notice under 2A:18-61.2(e)).
rent_increase_statewide_rent_control: No statewide rent control for apartments was found in the statutes. Municipal rent-control ordinances may apply (2A:18-61.1(f)). A 3.5% per 12-month cap applies only to manufactured-home sites (52:27D-287.13).
retaliation_rule: A landlord may not serve a notice to quit, sue for possession, or substantially change the tenancy (including refusing to renew without cause) as reprisal for the tenant trying to enforce rights under the lease or law, making a good-faith complaint to a government authority (after first telling the landlord and allowing reasonable time to fix it), or being involved in any lawful organization (2A:42-10.10). A notice to quit or substantial change without cause after such an act creates a rebuttable presumption of reprisal; no fixed time window applies (2A:42-10.12). The tenant can sue for damages and injunctive relief and wins any eviction case brought for these reasons (2A:42-10.10, 10.11). Does not apply to owner-occupied premises with no more than 2 rental units (2A:42-10.13).

deposit_max: If the rental agreement is for less than one year, the deposit may not exceed one month's rent. For an annual (one-year) agreement the statute sets no cap, but if the deposit is more than one month's rent the owner must pay the resident annual interest (passbook savings rate) on it. Prepaid last month's rent is not a deposit.
deposit_interest: Only where the agreement is annual and the deposit exceeds one month's rent (47-8-18(A)(1)): the owner must pay annual interest equal to the passbook rate. No interest on deposits up to one month's rent.
late_fee_rule: If the lease provides for a late fee, it may not exceed 5% of the rent for each rental period in default (reduced from 10% by Laws 2025, ch. 122, effective June 20, 2025). It is calculated on rent only, not deposits, fees or utilities, and the owner must give notice of the fee by the last day of the next rental period.
entry_notice: Unless otherwise agreed, 24 hours' written notice stating the intent to enter, the purpose, the date and a reasonable estimate of the time frame. Notice is not required for repairs or services within 7 days of a resident's request, or when accompanied by a public official or utility representative. Entry without consent is allowed in an emergency; the owner may not abuse the right of access.
month_to_month_tenant_notice: At least 30 days' written notice before the periodic rental date specified in the notice (47-8-37(B)).
month_to_month_landlord_notice: Same: at least 30 days' written notice before the periodic rental date specified in the notice (47-8-37(B)). For nonpayment the owner may end the agreement after a 3-day written notice (47-8-33(D)); for other breaches 7-day notice (47-8-33(A)).
rent_increase_notice: Month-to-month: written notice at least 30 days before the periodic rental date; fixed term: at least 30 days before the end of the term (47-8-15(F)). Increases to fees need 60 days' written notice (47-8-19.4).
rent_increase_statewide_rent_control: No statewide rent cap found in the Act.
retaliation_rule: An owner may not raise rent, cut services or bring or threaten a possession action because, within the previous six months, the resident complained to a code agency, organised, exercised rights (incl. written repair requests), made a fair-housing complaint, was in a lawsuit, testified or abated rent. Uniform increases applied to similar units are allowed. Violations: liable for two times the monthly rent and it is a defense to eviction.

deposit_max: 1 month's rent.
deposit_interest: Buildings with 6+ units: interest-bearing account at the prevailing rate; landlord may keep 1% a year as an administrative fee (Gen. Oblig. Law § 7-103). Smaller buildings: held in trust, no interest required.
late_fee_rule: Late fee only after rent is 5 days late, capped at the lesser of $50 or 5% of monthly rent. Separately, background/credit check fees are capped at actual cost or $20, whichever is less.
entry_notice: No general statewide statute; reasonable notice expected. In NYC, HPD rules require 24 hours' notice for inspections and 1 week for non-emergency repairs (28 RCNY 25-101).
month_to_month_tenant_notice: 1 month
month_to_month_landlord_notice: 30 days if tenancy under 1 year; 60 days for 1-2 years; 90 days for 2 years or more.
rent_increase_notice: Increases of 5% or more (or non-renewal) need the same 30/60/90-day notice as termination.
rent_increase_statewide_rent_control: No statewide cap. Rent stabilization covers many NYC units. Good Cause Eviction (RPL Art. 6-A, 2024) applies in NYC and opt-in localities: increases above the lesser of 10% or CPI + 5% are presumed unreasonable (not a hard cap; many exemptions).
retaliation_rule: Retaliation for good-faith complaints is prohibited; rebuttable presumption of retaliation for actions within 1 year of the complaint.

deposit_max: 2 weeks' rent (week-to-week), 1.5 months (month-to-month), 2 months (longer terms).
late_fee_rule: Only when rent is 5 or more calendar days late; one fee per late payment, capped at the greater of $15 or 5% of the monthly rent (weekly rent: greater of $4 or 5%).
entry_notice: No statute; follow the lease.
month_to_month_tenant_notice: 7 days
month_to_month_landlord_notice: 7 days
rent_increase_notice: No statutory notice period beyond ending the tenancy.
rent_increase_statewide_rent_control: No; local rent control is preempted (N.C.G.S. 42-14.1).
retaliation_rule: Retaliatory eviction is a defense when it follows a good-faith complaint or exercise of rights within 12 months.

deposit_max: One month's rent. Exceptions: up to two months' rent from an individual convicted of a felony offense as an incentive to rent to them, or from an individual who has had a judgment entered against them for violating a previous rental agreement (§ 47-16-07.1(1)). A separate pet security deposit (not for service or companion animals required as a disability accommodation) may be charged, up to the greater of $2,500 or two months' rent (§ 47-16-07.1(2)).
deposit_interest: Yes. The landlord must hold the deposit in a federally insured interest-bearing savings or checking account for the tenant's benefit, and pay the deposit and accrued interest on termination of the lease, less permitted deductions. No interest is owed if the period of occupancy was less than nine months (§ 47-16-07.1(1), (3)).
late_fee_rule: Chapter 47-16 sets no cap, grace period or other rule on residential late fees (other chapters of the code were not searched). Any late fee must come from the lease. A landlord may not charge a tenant a fee to accept cash, a check or a money order for rent or any other payment required under a lease (§ 47-16-20.1).
entry_notice: The landlord may enter at any time in an emergency, or if the landlord reasonably believes the tenant has abandoned the premises or is in substantial violation of the lease. Otherwise entry is allowed only during reasonable hours and in a reasonable manner, for inspection, necessary or agreed repairs and alterations, supplying services, or showing the unit to buyers, insurers, mortgagees, agents, tenants, workers or contractors. Unless impractical, the landlord must first notify the tenant and obtain consent (not to be unreasonably withheld) that identifies a time certain; consent is presumed if the tenant does not object after notice of entry at a time certain. Notice may be given in person, by posting in a conspicuous place for a reasonable period, or by any method that results in actual notice. The statute sets no fixed number of hours of notice. The landlord may not abuse access or use it to harass or intimidate (§ 47-16-07.3).
month_to_month_tenant_notice: Unless the parties agreed in writing to a longer period or different timing, at least one calendar month's written notice, given at any time; rent is due through the termination date (§ 47-16-15(2)). If the landlord changes lease terms under § 47-16-07, the tenant may terminate at the end of the month with at least 25 days' notice (§ 47-16-15(3)). A lease requiring more than one month's notice for residential property must state the requirement and have a space for the tenant's initials; if not initialed, the tenant may terminate on the last day of a month with one calendar month's notice (§ 47-16-15(4)).
month_to_month_landlord_notice: Same as the tenant: at least one calendar month's written notice at any time (§ 47-16-15(2)). For eviction, a tenant who holds over or fails to pay rent for three days after it is due may be evicted, but three days' written notice of intention to evict must first be given before proceedings are started; the same 3-day notice applies where the tenant violates a material term of the written lease. Notice may be served like a summons or, if the party cannot be found, posted conspicuously on the premises by the sheriff or a process server (§§ 47-32-01(4), (5), (6), (8), 47-32-02). A residential lease for a specified term of two months or more cannot be renewed under an automatic renewal clause unless the landlord gave written notice of the clause (personally or by first-class mail) at least 30 days before expiry; otherwise the lease expires and converts to month-to-month (§ 47-16-06.1).
rent_increase_notice: For a month-to-month lease, the landlord may change terms (including rent) effective at the end of a month by giving written notice at least 30 days before the end of the month. The notice may be served in any reasonable manner that actually informs the tenant. If the tenant stays after the month ends, the new terms become part of the lease. The tenant may terminate at the end of the month by giving at least 25 days' notice (§§ 47-16-07, 47-16-15(3)). The statute sets no cap on the amount of an increase.
rent_increase_statewide_rent_control: Rent control is prohibited: a political subdivision may not enact, maintain or enforce an ordinance or resolution that would control the amount of rent charged for leasing private residential or commercial property (§ 47-16-02.1).
retaliation_citation: N.D.C.C. ch. 47-16 (no general retaliation provision found). § 47-16-17.1(10) bars refusing to rent, or otherwise retaliating, solely because a tenant exercised the right to terminate a lease as a domestic violence victim.

deposit_max: No statutory cap.
deposit_interest: If the deposit exceeds $50 or one month's rent (whichever is greater), the excess earns 5% yearly interest when the tenant stays 6+ months.
late_fee_rule: No Ohio statute found that caps residential late fees or sets a rent grace period; the lease sets the fee (ORC 5321.06). A court may refuse to enforce a lease clause it finds unconscionable (ORC 5321.14), but no late-fee-specific test was found. Sections searched: ORC 5321.01-5321.06, 5321.13-5321.19, 1923.02, 1923.04.
entry_notice: 24 hours' notice and reasonable times, except emergencies.
month_to_month_tenant_notice: 30 days
month_to_month_landlord_notice: 30 days
rent_increase_notice: No statutory notice period beyond ending a periodic tenancy.
rent_increase_statewide_rent_control: No.
retaliation_rule: Landlord may not raise rent, cut services or evict because a tenant complained to authorities or the landlord or joined a tenant union.

deposit_max: No statutory cap on the amount of a security deposit found in 41 O.S. §§ 101-136. 'Deposit' means money or other property required by a landlord from a tenant as security, to be returned on termination less deductions properly made under the Act (§ 102(2)). The deposit must be kept in an escrow account in an Oklahoma federally insured financial institution; misappropriation is unlawful and punishable by county jail up to six months and a fine up to twice the amount misappropriated (§ 115(A)). On termination the deposit may be applied to accrued rent and damages from the tenant's noncompliance with the Act and rental agreement, itemized in a written statement (§ 115(B)). A tenant may not deduct the deposit from last month's rent unless the rental agreement provides otherwise (§ 115(F)).
deposit_interest: No interest: the balance is returned 'without interest' (§ 115(B)). The deposit must be held in an Oklahoma escrow account (§ 115(A)).
late_fee_rule: No provision on residential late fees found in 41 O.S. §§ 101-136 or elsewhere in Title 41 (the whole title text was searched for 'late fee' / 'late charge'). Any late fee must come from the lease. Not searched: other titles of the Oklahoma Statutes.
entry_notice: A tenant may not unreasonably withhold consent to the landlord entering to inspect, make necessary or agreed repairs, supply services or show the unit (§ 128(A)). Except in an emergency or where it is impracticable, the landlord must give the tenant at least one (1) day's notice of intent to enter and may enter only at reasonable times (§ 128(C)). Entry without consent is allowed in an emergency (§ 128(B)). The landlord may not abuse the right of access or use it to harass (§ 128(C)). Remedy for unlawful or harassing entry: injunction or termination on written notice, plus actual damages (§ 124(A)).
month_to_month_tenant_notice: Written notice at least 30 days before the effective date; the 30 days run from the date notice is served (§ 111(A), (E)). Notice must be served personally (or on a family member over 12, or posted plus certified mail) (§ 111(E)).
month_to_month_landlord_notice: Same: written notice at least 30 days before the effective date, served as provided in § 111(E) (§ 111(A)). Nonpayment: tenancy may be terminated if the tenant does not pay within 5 days after written notice of the landlord's demand for payment (§ 131(B)). Material breach by tenant: written notice that the agreement will end not less than 15 days after receipt unless remedied within 10 days (§ 132(B)). Tenancy less than month-to-month: 7 days (§ 111(B)). A victim of domestic violence, sexual violence or stalking may terminate without penalty by written notice and a protective order of an incident, given within 30 days of the incident unless the landlord waives the period (§ 111(F)).
rent_increase_notice: No statute found requiring advance notice of a rent increase in 41 O.S. §§ 101-136. Rent is payable at the time and place agreed (§ 109(B)). For a month-to-month tenancy the only notice rule found is the 30-day termination notice (§ 111(A)).
rent_increase_statewide_rent_control: No statewide rent control found in the Act. 2026 bill SB 1296 (90-day notice, 7% + CPI cap) did not advance past Senate committee referral (oklegislature.gov bill page, checked 2026-10-22).
retaliation_rule: No general retaliation statute found in 41 O.S. §§ 101-136. The only anti-retaliation text found is § 113.3: a landlord may not deny, refuse to renew or terminate a tenancy because the applicant, tenant or household member is a victim or alleged victim of domestic violence, sexual violence or stalking, and may not deny a tenancy or retaliate against a tenant who previously terminated a rental agreement for that reason.

deposit_max: No statutory cap in ORS 90.300; a landlord cannot require a new or increased deposit in the first year of tenancy (except for an agreed change such as adding a pet), and must allow at least 3 months to pay one after that.
late_fee_rule: Only if rent is not received by the 4th day of the rental period and the written lease states the fee, its type and amount, and when it is due; the fee may not exceed a reasonable flat amount (customary in the market) once per period, or a per-day amount from day 5 capped at 6% of that flat amount, or 5% of the rent per 5-day period from day 5. Unpaid late fees alone are not grounds for a nonpayment eviction.
entry_notice: At least 24 hours' actual notice, at reasonable times; no notice for emergencies (tenant told within 24 hours after an emergency entry in their absence) or for entering to make repairs the tenant requested in writing (that permission lasts 7 days).
month_to_month_tenant_notice: 30 days written notice (10 days for week-to-week).
month_to_month_landlord_notice: 30 days written notice without cause only during the first year of occupancy; after that only for tenant cause, or with 90 days notice for a qualifying landlord reason (demolition or conversion, repairs that make the home unfit, landlord or immediate family moving in, sale to a buyer who will live there) plus one month's rent paid with the notice; landlords with an ownership interest in 4 or fewer units are exempt from the payment.
rent_increase_notice: No increase in the first year; afterwards 90 days written notice (7 days for week-to-week), at most once per 12 months, and no more than the annual cap: lesser of 10% or 7% plus CPI (West Region), published by DAS each September. Cap is 9.5% for 2026 and 10% for 2027 (DAS announcement Sept 28, 2026). The notice must state the increase, the new rent and the effective date. Units whose first certificate of occupancy is under 15 years old, and some subsidized units, are exempt from the cap.
rent_increase_statewide_rent_control: Yes; statewide annual rent cap (ORS 90.323, 90.324). Violation: 3 months' rent plus damages.
retaliation_rule: Landlord may not raise rent, cut services, serve a termination notice or threaten eviction because a tenant complained in good faith to the landlord or to a government agency (housing/health code, discrimination), joined or organized a tenants' union, testified against the landlord, won an eviction case in the last 6 months, or asserted any legal tenant right; retaliation is a defense to eviction.

deposit_max: 2 months' rent in the first year; 1 month's rent from the second year on.
deposit_interest: Deposits over $100 must be held in a separate escrow account; from the third year of the lease it must earn interest, paid to the tenant yearly minus a 1% landlord fee (68 P.S. § 250.511b). Deposits of $100 or less: no escrow or interest.
late_fee_rule: No provision on residential rent late fees (no cap, no required grace period, no required notice) was found in Pennsylvania's Landlord and Tenant Act of 1951 (68 P.S. 250.101 et seq., all articles read), so any late fee depends on the lease. Local ordinances (e.g. Philadelphia, Pittsburgh) and other Pennsylvania statutes were not searched.
late_fee_citation: Landlord and Tenant Act of 1951, Act of Apr. 6, 1951, P.L. 69, No. 20 (68 P.S. 250.101 et seq.), full text searched; no late-fee section found
entry_notice: No statute; follow the lease.
month_to_month_landlord_notice: Notice to quit: 15 days (lease of 1 year or less / indefinite) or 30 days (over 1 year) for eviction; tenants can waive this in the lease.
rent_increase_notice: No statutory notice period.
rent_increase_statewide_rent_control: No.

deposit_max: A landlord may not demand or receive a security deposit, however denominated, worth more than one month's periodic rent (34-18-19(a)). A landlord renting a furnished apartment whose furniture was worth $5,000 or more when the lease was signed may charge a separate furniture security deposit (34-18-19(e)); the statute states no cap on that furniture deposit. No rental agreement may waive the section (34-18-19(h)).
deposit_interest: No interest or separate-account requirement found in 34-18-19.
late_fee_rule: No provision capping late fees or requiring a grace period found in Chapter 34-18. Fees beyond rent must be disclosed in the lease in the same section as the rent disclosure, with an indication that additional fees may apply; if there is no written lease the landlord must list all such fees in writing, and a change in fees must be disclosed in writing at least 30 days before it takes effect. A tenant may recover any fees paid that were not disclosed as required (34-18-15(a)(1), (2), (5)). A landlord may not send the written nonpayment demand until rent is 15 days in arrears (34-18-35(a)). A landlord may not charge a convenience fee on a tenant's rent payment unless it accepts a form of payment that carries no convenience fee (34-18-61). A landlord may not require a rental application fee, except an actual-cost charge for an official state criminal background check or credit report under the limits of 34-18-59.
entry_notice: The landlord must give the tenant at least two days' notice of intent to enter, except in an emergency or where giving notice is impracticable, and may enter only at reasonable times. The landlord may not abuse the right of access or use it to harass the tenant. A tenant may not unreasonably withhold consent to entry for inspection, agreed repairs, services or showings. Entry without consent is allowed in an emergency or, during a tenant absence of more than seven days, when reasonably necessary to protect the property. The landlord has no other right of access except under a court order, as permitted by 34-18-39, or where the tenant has abandoned or surrendered the premises.
month_to_month_tenant_notice: Written notice delivered to the other party at least 30 days before the termination date specified in the notice (34-18-37(b)); week-to-week tenancies need at least 10 days (34-18-37(a)). The notice must be in a form substantially similar to 34-18-56(c).
month_to_month_landlord_notice: Same: at least 30 days' written notice for a month-to-month tenancy (34-18-37(b)). For unpaid rent, the landlord must send a written demand once rent is 15 days in arrears giving the tenant 5 days from mailing to pay; an eviction action may be filed no earlier than the 6th day after mailing (34-18-35(a)-(b)).
rent_increase_notice: A landlord must give written notice of a rent increase at least 60 days before it takes effect, and at least 120 days to month-to-month tenants over age 62; independent living, assisted living and congregate care facilities are excluded, and a longer notice period required by other state or federal law or housing program rules is not shortened (34-18-16.1, effective June 24, 2024).
rent_increase_statewide_rent_control: No statewide rent cap found in Chapter 34-18.
retaliation_rule: A landlord may not retaliate by increasing rent, decreasing services, or bringing or threatening an action for possession because the tenant complained to a housing-code enforcement agency about a violation materially affecting health and safety, complained to the landlord of a violation of the landlord's maintenance duties (34-18-22), organized or joined a tenants' union, or used any other lawful right or remedy. Evidence of a complaint within 6 months before the alleged retaliation creates a presumption of retaliation, which does not arise if the tenant complained after notice of a proposed rent increase or loss of services. The landlord may still seek possession if the violation was caused primarily by the tenant's lack of reasonable care, the tenant is in default in rent, or code compliance requires work that would deprive the tenant of the unit and relocation requirements are met.

deposit_max: No cap on the amount in the Residential Landlord and Tenant Act.
late_fee_rule: No late-fee cap in the Residential Landlord and Tenant Act; late charges count as 'rent' under the Act's definition, so they must be agreed in the rental agreement.
entry_notice: At least 24 hours' notice and entry only at reasonable times. Exceptions: emergencies; regularly scheduled services (filters, pest treatment) 9 a.m.-6 p.m. if conspicuously written in the lease and announced before entering; tenant-requested services 8 a.m.-8 p.m. after announcing. Landlord may not abuse access or use it to harass the tenant. Tenant may not change locks without permission.
month_to_month_tenant_notice: 30 days' written notice before the termination date (7 days for week-to-week)
month_to_month_landlord_notice: 30 days' written notice before the termination date (7 days for week-to-week)
rent_increase_notice: No rent-increase notice period in the Residential Landlord and Tenant Act; increases above fair-market value can be retaliatory after a protected complaint (27-40-910).
retaliation_rule: Landlord may not raise rent above fair-market value, cut essential services, or sue for possession because the tenant complained to a code agency or to the landlord about a violation of the Act. Liability up to 3 months' rent or treble actual damages (whichever is greater) plus attorney fees. Tenant must give written notice of the defense within 10 days after service of the Rule to Vacate.

deposit_max: 1 month's rent. A larger deposit is allowed only by agreement of landlord and tenant where special conditions pose a danger to maintenance of the premises. Any money deposited to secure the rental agreement counts as a security deposit, however it is labelled (§ 43-32-6.1).
deposit_interest: No interest requirement in §§ 43-32-6.1 or 43-32-24.
late_fee_rule: Chapter 43-32 contains no cap, grace period or other rule on residential late fees (other chapters of the code were not searched). Any late fee must come from the lease.
entry_notice: Except in an emergency or where notice is impracticable, the landlord must give reasonable notice of intent to enter and enter only at reasonable times. 24 hours' written notice is presumed reasonable unless the lease sets other notice methods or times. The notice must state the date(s) of entry, a time window during normal business hours, the purpose of entry, and how the tenant can ask to reschedule. The statute sets no specific penalty.
month_to_month_tenant_notice: For a hiring with no agreed term, either party must give notice of intent to terminate at least as long before the end of the term as the term itself, not exceeding one month; for month-to-month, at least one month before the end of the monthly term. The statute does not say the notice must be in writing.
month_to_month_landlord_notice: Same one-month rule for a month-to-month hiring (§ 43-32-15). Separately, a landlord may end a fixed-term lease early if the tenant uses the premises contrary to the lease or does not make repairs the tenant is bound to make within a reasonable time after request (§ 43-32-18).
rent_increase_notice: On a month-to-month lease the landlord may change the terms, including the rent, by written notice given at least 30 days before the end of the month; the change takes effect at the end of the month if the tenant stays. The tenant may end the lease effective the first day of the next month by giving notice within 15 days of receiving the notice of change. The statute covers month-to-month leases only; a fixed-term lease cannot be changed by this notice.
rent_increase_statewide_rent_control: No statewide rent control provision found in chapter 43-32. Raising rent above fair market value after a tenant's protected complaint can be retaliation (§ 43-32-27).
retaliation_rule: A tenant of residential property has a cause of action if the landlord increases rent above fair market value, decreases electric, gas, water or sewer service, or gives notice to vacate not based on a lease breach, after the tenant (1) complained in good faith to a governmental agency about a housing or building code violation materially affecting health and safety and the landlord received written notice of it, (2) gave the landlord written notice of a repair condition under § 43-32-9, or (3) organized or joined a tenants' union. It is a defense that the notice to vacate came more than 180 days after that event; not renewing a written lease at expiration is not retaliation. The tenant gets the remedies in § 43-32-6 and the court may award reasonable attorney's fees.

deposit_max: No statutory cap (Tenn. Code Ann. § 66-28-301 sets none).
late_fee_rule: No late fee until after a 5-day grace period (day rent is due counts as day 1; extended to next business day if day 5 is a Sunday or holiday); fee capped at 10% of the rent past due.
entry_notice: No general advance-notice period; tenant may not unreasonably refuse access. For showing to prospective tenants in the last 30 days of the lease (if the lease allows), 24 hours' notice. Emergency entry allowed.
month_to_month_tenant_notice: 30 days written notice before the periodic rental date (10 days for week-to-week).
month_to_month_landlord_notice: 30 days written notice before the periodic rental date (10 days for week-to-week).
rent_increase_statewide_rent_control: No; local governments may not control rent (Tenn. Code Ann. 66-35-102).
retaliation_rule: Landlord may not retaliate by raising rent, cutting services or bringing/threatening a possession action because the tenant complained to the landlord of a violation (the statute cross-references § 66-28-301) or used remedies under the Act (exceptions: tenant-caused code violation, tenant in rent default, code compliance that requires alteration, remodeling or demolition).

deposit_max: No statutory cap.
late_fee_rule: Late fee only if rent remains unpaid 2 full days after the due date, must be in a written lease and reasonable. Safe harbor: up to 12% of monthly rent (buildings with 4 or fewer units) or 10% (more than 4 units).
entry_notice: No statute; entry rules come from the lease.
month_to_month_tenant_notice: 1 month (unless the lease says otherwise)
month_to_month_landlord_notice: 1 month (unless the lease says otherwise)
rent_increase_notice: No statutory notice period beyond ending the tenancy; follow the lease.
rent_increase_statewide_rent_control: No; local rent control is preempted except in declared disasters (Local Gov't Code 214.902).
retaliation_rule: No retaliation for 6 months after a tenant in good faith requests repairs or exercises legal rights.

deposit_max: No statutory cap. Any non-refundable portion of a deposit must be stated in writing to the renter when the deposit is taken (57-17-2).
deposit_interest: false
late_fee_rule: A late fee may not exceed the greater of 10% of the agreed rent or $75. Fees not in the rental agreement can't be charged unless the tenancy is month-to-month and the landlord gives 15 days' notice of the charge.
entry_notice: At least 24 hours' notice, unless the rental agreement provides otherwise.
month_to_month_landlord_notice: Notice served at least 15 calendar days before the end of the month or rental period.

deposit_max: No statutory cap on the amount of a security deposit found in 9 V.S.A. chapter 137. A 'security deposit' is any advance, deposit or prepaid rent, however named, that is refundable to the tenant at the end of the tenancy; its function is to secure the tenant's obligations to pay rent and maintain the unit (§ 4461(a)). The landlord may retain it only for nonpayment of rent, damage beyond normal wear and tear (or beyond the tenant's control), unpaid utility or other charges the tenant had to pay directly, and expenses to remove articles the tenant abandoned (§ 4461(b)). 'Normal wear and tear' is defined in § 4451(5). A separate bill that would have capped deposits at two months' rent (H.772, 2026) failed in the Senate and did not become law.
deposit_interest: No statewide interest or separate-account requirement found in chapter 137. A town or municipality may adopt a supplemental ordinance, which may authorize interest on deposits but may not limit how a deposit is held (§ 4461(g)).
late_fee_rule: No provision on residential late fees found in 9 V.S.A. chapter 137. Rent is payable without demand or notice at the time and place agreed (§ 4455(a)), so any late fee must come from the lease. Separately, a landlord may not charge an application fee to apply for a residential rental (§ 4456a(a)).
entry_notice: A landlord may enter with the tenant's consent, which the tenant may not unreasonably withhold. Otherwise the landlord may enter only between 9:00 A.M. and 9:00 P.M. on at least 48 hours' notice, and only to inspect the premises, make necessary or agreed repairs, alterations or improvements, supply agreed services, or show the unit to prospective or actual purchasers, mortgagees, tenants, workers or contractors. The landlord may enter without consent or notice only where there is a reasonable belief of imminent danger to a person or property. Illegal lockouts and utility shut-offs are prohibited (§ 4463).
month_to_month_tenant_notice: 9 V.S.A. chapter 137 states no notice period for a tenant ending a tenancy (§ 4467 sets only the landlord's notice periods); follow the notice terms in the lease.
month_to_month_landlord_notice: No cause is needed only if there is NO written rental agreement and rent is monthly: at least 60 days' actual notice if the tenant has lived there continuously 2 years or less, at least 90 days if more than 2 years (§ 4467(c)(1)); weekly rent: 21 days (§ 4467(c)(2)). With a written rental agreement, a no-cause notice must be given at least 30 days before the end of the stated term if the tenancy has lasted 2 years or less, and at least 60 days before the end if more than 2 years (week-to-week written agreement: 7 days) (§ 4467(e)). Nonpayment of rent: at least 14 days' actual notice, and the tenancy does not end if the tenant pays the rent due through the end of the rental period (§ 4467(a)). Breach of a material term or of chapter duties: at least 30 days (§ 4467(b)(1)); criminal activity, illegal drug activity or violence threatening other residents: at least 14 days (§ 4467(b)(2)). Shared-home room rental: 15 days if rent is monthly, 7 days if weekly (§ 4467(h)). The notice must state the termination date (§ 4467(f)); 'actual notice' means written notice hand-delivered or mailed to the last known address, presumed received 3 days after mailing (§ 4451(1)). An eviction case must be started within 60 days after the termination date (§ 4467(k)).
rent_increase_notice: A rent increase takes effect on the first day of the rental period that follows at least 60 days' actual notice to the tenant (§ 4455(b)). For privately owned age-restricted residential property not licensed under 33 V.S.A. ch. 71 or 8 V.S.A. ch. 151, the owner must give 60 days' written notice on the state form to residents and the Department of Housing and Community Development; a rent increase without that notice is ineffective and unenforceable (§ 4468a).
rent_increase_statewide_rent_control: No statewide rent cap found in 9 V.S.A. chapter 137. A bill with rent-increase limits (H.772, 2026) failed in the Senate and did not become law.
retaliation_rule: A landlord may not retaliate, by establishing or changing rental terms or by bringing or threatening an action, against a tenant who complained to a government agency about a health or safety violation of building, housing or health regulations, complained to the landlord of a violation of chapter 137, or organized or joined a tenants' union (§ 4465(a)). A tenant can recover damages and attorney's fees, and may raise it as a defense to an action for possession (§ 4465(b)). If the landlord serves a termination notice on any ground other than nonpayment of rent within 90 days after a municipal or state notice that the premises violate health or safety rules, there is a rebuttable presumption the termination is retaliatory (§ 4465(c)).

deposit_max: 2 months' periodic rent (security deposit however named). Security deposit plus damage-insurance and renter's-insurance premiums paid before the tenancy starts may not exceed 2 months' rent in total.
late_fee_rule: Only if provided for in the written rental agreement; capped at the lesser of 10% of the periodic rent or 10% of the remaining balance due.
entry_notice: Notice of intent to enter and entry only at reasonable times, except in an emergency or where impractical. At least 72 hours' notice for routine maintenance the tenant did not request. Landlord may not abuse access or use it to harass the tenant.
month_to_month_tenant_notice: 30 days (written, before the next rent due date), unless the rental agreement provides a different period
month_to_month_landlord_notice: 30 days (written, before the next rent due date), unless the rental agreement provides a different period; 60 days for certain mass non-renewals in multifamily premises
rent_increase_notice: Landlords owning more than four rental units (or >10% interest in more than four) must give written notice of a rent increase for the next term, and of non-renewal, at least 60 days before the lease term ends, to tenants with a renewal option or auto-renewal clause. An amended version effective July 1, 2027 raises the rent-increase notice to 90 days.
retaliation_rule: Landlord may not raise rent, cut services, or threaten/bring an eviction or termination because the tenant complained to a housing-code agency, complained or sued under the Act, joined a tenants' organization, or testified against the landlord. Tenant may recover actual damages and raise retaliation as a defense. (Expanded version effective January 1, 2027.)

deposit_max: No statewide cap found. A deposit may be collected only with a written lease and a signed, dated move-in checklist describing the unit's condition; without the checklist the landlord is liable for the whole deposit. Deposits go in a Washington trust account and the tenant gets a receipt. On written request, the tenant may pay deposits, nonrefundable fees and last month's rent in installments (2 or 3 months) unless they total no more than 25% of the first month's rent. A fee is refundable unless the written lease clearly calls it nonrefundable.
late_fee_rule: No late fee for rent paid within 5 days after the due date; after that, late fees may run from the day after the due date. A lease clause agreeing to earlier late fees is prohibited.
entry_notice: At least 2 days' written notice stating the date(s) and time window plus a phone number for objections, and entry only at reasonable times; 1 day's notice to show the unit to buyers or tenants. No notice needed in an emergency or abandonment, or where notice is impracticable. No harassment or excessive showings.
month_to_month_tenant_notice: 20 days' written notice before the end of a rental period
month_to_month_landlord_notice: Only for a 'cause' listed in RCW 59.18.650, with the notice that cause requires (a 6–12 month initial lease that rolls to month-to-month may be ended without cause at the end of the initial term with 60 days' written notice).
rent_increase_notice: At least 90 days' written notice of any rent increase (30 days for income-based subsidized tenancies), using the state-required notice form; an increase cannot take effect before the lease term ends.
rent_increase_statewide_rent_control: Yes (since May 7, 2025): no increase in the first 12 months of a tenancy, then at most 7% + CPI or 10%, whichever is less, per 12 months; the Department of Commerce publishes the yearly figure. Exempt: units whose first certificate of occupancy is 12 years old or newer, some nonprofit/public/low-income housing, and some owner-occupied homes and 2–4 unit buildings.
retaliation_rule: Landlord may not retaliate (eviction, rent increase, reduced services, added obligations) for good-faith complaints to authorities or asserting rights; action within 90 days is presumed retaliatory (rebuttable), except when the tenant is behind on rent or in breach.

late_fee_rule: No statewide cap or grace period found in Articles 6 and 6A. The security-deposit statute refers to "reasonable charges for late payment of rent specified in the rental agreement", so a late charge must be in the lease and reasonable.
month_to_month_tenant_notice: Written notice for one full rental period before the end of a period (one month for a month-to-month tenancy); a year-to-year tenancy needs written notice at least three months before the end of the year. A different period fixed by special agreement in the lease controls.
month_to_month_landlord_notice: Same as the tenant: written notice for one full rental period before the end of a period (one month for a month-to-month tenancy); a year-to-year tenancy needs written notice at least three months before the end of the year. A different period fixed by special agreement controls; no notice is needed for a fixed term that ends at a certain time.

deposit_max: No statutory cap on the deposit amount in Wis. Stat. 704.28 or ATCP 134.06. Any rent prepayment above one month's prepaid rent counts as a 'security deposit' and must be returned under the same rules (ATCP 134.06(2) note). Before accepting a deposit the landlord must tell the tenant in writing they may inspect the unit and report pre-existing damage, or request a list of damage charged to the previous tenant, by a deadline at least 7 days after the tenancy starts (ATCP 134.06(1)). Wisconsin law has no deposit-interest or separate-account rule in these sections.
deposit_interest: No interest requirement in Wis. Stat. 704.28 or ATCP 134.06.
deposit_citation: Wis. Stat. 704.28; Wis. Admin. Code ATCP 134.06
late_fee_rule: A landlord may charge a late rent fee or penalty only if the rental agreement specifically provides for it. Before charging a late fee the landlord must apply any rent prepayments received from that tenant against the rent owed, and may not charge a fee or penalty for non-payment of a late fee. The rules cited set no dollar or percentage cap and no grace period. For the 5-day pay-or-vacate eviction notice, past-due late fees count as rent (Wis. Stat. 704.17(1g)).
late_fee_citation: Wis. Admin. Code ATCP 134.09(8); Wis. Stat. 704.17(1g)
entry_notice: Entry is allowed only to inspect, make repairs or show the unit to prospective tenants or purchasers, on advance notice and at reasonable times, for no longer than reasonably needed. Advance notice means at least 12 hours unless the tenant, once told of the proposed entry, agrees to a shorter time. No notice is needed if the tenant requests or consents in advance knowing the time, there is a health or safety emergency, or the tenant is absent and the landlord reasonably believes entry is needed to protect the premises from damage. The landlord must announce their presence before entering and identify themselves on request. A lease may add other entry rights only through a separate signed 'NONSTANDARD RENTAL PROVISIONS' document.
entry_citation: Wis. Admin. Code ATCP 134.09(2); Wis. Stat. 704.05(2)
month_to_month_tenant_notice: At least 28 days' written notice, ending at the end of a rental period (periodic tenancy or tenancy at will). Rent payable on a basis shorter than monthly: notice at least equal to the rent-paying period.
month_to_month_landlord_notice: Same 28 days' written notice for a periodic tenancy or tenancy at will. For unpaid rent, a month-to-month tenant can be given notice to pay rent or vacate within at least 5 days; a month-to-month tenancy is also terminated if, while the tenant is in default on rent, the landlord gives at least 14 days' notice to vacate. For other lease breaches the landlord can require the tenant to cure or vacate within at least 5 days, or give 14 days' notice to vacate if the same kind of breach recurs within a year. Notice must be given by a method in s. 704.21.
rent_increase_statewide_rent_control: No statewide rent control or rent-increase notice rule found in ch. 704 or ATCP 134. Cities, villages, towns and counties may not regulate the amount of rent or fees charged for a residential rental unit (Wis. Stat. 66.1015(1)), with exceptions for housing they own or operate. A landlord may not increase rent in retaliation for protected tenant conduct (Wis. Stat. 704.45).
retaliation_rule: A residential landlord may not raise rent, cut services, start an action for possession, refuse to renew a lease, or threaten any of these if the tenant shows by a preponderance of the evidence the action would not occur but for retaliation for: a good-faith complaint about a premises defect to an elected official or local housing code agency; complaining to the landlord about a violation of s. 704.07 or the housing code; or exercising a legal right relating to residential tenancies. The landlord may still sue for possession for unpaid rent (other than a prohibited rent increase), and the section does not cover defects caused by the tenant's negligence or improper use (704.45). The rules also bar terminating a tenancy, refusing renewal or constructively evicting a tenant in retaliation for reporting a code or ATCP 134 violation, joining a tenant union, or asserting rights under state or local law (ATCP 134.09(5)). No fixed look-back presumption period.
retaliation_citation: Wis. Stat. 704.45; Wis. Admin. Code ATCP 134.09(5)

deposit_max: No statutory cap. A rental agreement must state whether any portion of the deposit is nonrefundable, and written notice of that fact must also be given to the renter when the deposit is taken (§ 1-21-1207).
deposit_interest: No. The balance of the deposit and prepaid rent is delivered or mailed "without interest" (§ 1-21-1208(a)).
late_fee_citation: W.S. 1-21-1201 to 1-21-1211 (no late-fee provision found; other titles of the code were not searched)
entry_notice: The statute sets no notice period or hours for landlord entry. It only provides that a renter may not unreasonably deny access, refuse entry or withhold consent to entry by the owner, agent or manager to make repairs, inspect the unit, or show it for rent or sale (§ 1-21-1205(a)(iii)); such a violation can support a forcible entry and detainer action (§ 1-21-1002(a)(vi)). Any notice terms must come from the lease.
month_to_month_landlord_notice: No statutory notice period for ending a month-to-month tenancy was found in Title 1 art. 12 or Title 34. For nonpayment, an eviction action may be brought against a tenant holding over after failing to pay rent three days after it is due (§ 1-21-1002(a)(i)); the landlord must first give the tenant written notice to leave the premises, served at least 3 days before the action is commenced, by leaving a copy with the defendant or at the usual place of abode or business if the defendant cannot be found (§ 1-21-1003). The same procedure applies to renters violating the duties in §§ 1-21-1204 or 1-21-1205 (§ 1-21-1002(a)(vi)).
rent_increase_statewide_rent_control: No rent-increase notice requirement and no rent control provision found in W.S. 1-21-1201 to 1-21-1211 (other titles not searched).
retaliation_citation: W.S. 1-21-1201 to 1-21-1211 (no retaliation provision found; the Wyoming Safe Homes Act, § 1-21-1303(c), bars terminating a tenancy based solely on victim status)
